subject: Insurance
title: AIG and the 2008 Financial Crisis
description: A 60-second lesson on AIG and the 2008 Financial Crisis.

hook.text: AIG sold insurance on mortgage-backed securities without enough reserves.

buildup.text: AIG's financial products unit had sold credit default swaps—essentially insurance on bonds—to banks worldwide.

discovery.text: When the housing market collapsed, every swap triggered a payout.

twist.text: The US government bailed out AIG for $182 billion—the largest bailout in history.

climax.text: AIG proved that insurance without proper reserves is just a promise that can't be kept.

punchline.text: $182 billion bailout. AIG sold insurance it couldn't afford to pay.

quiz.question: Why did AIG need a government bailout?
options: It sold insurance on mortgage securities without enough reserves
